rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials went off track (0 finishes). Progress was only 0.11 to 0.16, with one line-loss event per run and max_error about 0.06 to 0.067 m. That max_error sits right at the off-track limit of max(0.06, 0.03 + 0.03) = 0.06 m. Steering oscillation was highest on the s-bend (0.15), which points to over-correction in bends. The robot is losing the line in the first curves, so the stability margin is the first problem. Following the Evaluator's guidance, I lowered base_speed from 1.6 to 1.3 to give the controller more time to correct on tight bends. I also made a moderate gain change: kp from 3.0 to 2.5 to reduce over-correction, and kd from 0.15 to 0.3 to damp the oscillation that the s-bend shows. Sensor geometry and sensor_weights are unchanged, so the sensor layout is not a variable in this race. Expected result: the robot stays on the tape through the s-bend and slalom, line_loss_events falls to 0 or near it, and progress rises well above 0.2. Completion within 3 s may still be out of reach at this speed. If the next race completes with small rms_error but completion_time above 3 s, I will raise base_speed toward 1.9 with kp and kd held. Hypotheses to test: (1) the line loss is caused by speed in bends, not by sensor coverage; (2) kd 0.3 reduces the steering_oscillation seen on the s-bend. Measurements requested: per-track progress, line_loss_events, max_error, and steering_oscillation, plus completion_time for any completed run.
